clue.text: Abandon computers? You're mad!

parts.note: to come off something, like a drug or a diet, is to give it up
IT, information technology, is the world of computers

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a friend's plan to give up using computers.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief, telling someone that what they say is nonsense.

clue.text: A policeman keeling over has swallowed revolting drink

indicators.note: the reversed letters take the next piece inside them, as a mouth takes in food
something keeling over is turned upside down, so in a down clue these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: PC is a police constable
people in revolt are up in arms, so up

explanation.surface: A constable collapses after downing some disgusting beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'keeling over' tips the first two pieces upside down together; 'revolting' means rising up, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of tea, the informal British word for a hot drink.

clue.text: Drivel getting mum down

parts.note: ma is another word for mother
down and under both mean below

explanation.surface: A mother's spirits fall as someone talks rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to talk aimlessly and rambling, the verb sense of maunder.

clue.text: Exaggerate about cast

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something
to cast is to throw, or pitch

explanation.surface: A fishing story that grows bigger about the size of the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate a case or claim is to make it more than it is, to exaggerate.

clue.text: Pan scrubber used by cat that's ruined waffle?

definitions.text: Pan scrubber used by cat that's ruined waffle?

parts.words: Pan scrubber used by cat that's ruined waffle?
parts.note: pan is slang for the face, so the scrubber is a washcloth for it; and a cat (a person) who has ruined things may try to save face with waffle, which British slang also calls flannel

explanation.surface: A kitchen scourer is grabbed by a cat that has spoiled the breakfast waffles.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture of pans and waffles misleads: pan means face, and flannel is British slang for evasive waffle as well as the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square of towelling cloth used for washing one's face, the British word for a washcloth.

clue.text: Pull north out of shopping centre

indicators.note: out of means the following letter is taken away from the place named

parts.note: a town is where one goes to the shops

explanation.surface: Someone drags a trolley out of the northern end of the mall.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow a vehicle is to pull it along behind another.

clue.text: Trail about to be followed by a policeman

indicators.note: says the next piece comes after the first
about means turned round, so the word for trail runs backwards

parts.note: to trail something behind you is to drag it

explanation.surface: A detective's trail is picked up by one officer after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda is the Irish police force, and a garda is one of its officers.

clue.text: Theory held by some colleagues, speculatively

indicators.note: held by some says the answer is a run of letters kept inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An idea quietly entertained by a few workmates, with no proof.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Theory held' as the definition; 'held' belongs with 'by some' as the signal for the hidden run, and 'Theory' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is a conjecture, an unproved theory about what is true.

clue.text: After fare is reduced by half, pay for N flight

indicators.note: says the next piece comes after the first
only the second half of the word fare is kept

parts.note: to treat someone is to pay for them

explanation.surface: Once the ticket price is halved, someone pays for a friend's air trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed N is an OCR slip for 'a'. 'Flight' means running away, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal or flight from danger.

clue.text: Nancy's naked? Untrue, alas, but not completely changed completely changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters are rearranged
the last letter of alas is dropped, so it is not given whole

explanation.surface: A rumour about a woman called Nancy posing nude is denied.
explanation.walkthrough: The page repeats 'completely changed'; the second copy is a printing slip. Nancy is the French city, so French for naked is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for in the natural state, naked; Nancy is a city in France.

clue.text: Name couple upset? He's composed

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair are upset over a name, while one man stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like calm, but it means someone who wrote music.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a French composer, so he composed music.

clue.text: Like bread married couple scoffed?

parts.note: W and H stand for wife and husband
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A husband and wife polish off a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten means made of wheat, as bread usually is.

clue.text: Make sense of answer given by theologian at university

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity
a student at university is up, in British usage

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar on campus supplies the reply to a question.
explanation.definitionFit: If a story adds up, it makes sense and is consistent.

clue.text: Does height in imperial units, given handy reference

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the units of length

parts.note: feet are imperial units of length
does means acts, as in performs

explanation.surface: A form records someone's height in feet and inches as a quick guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact sheet is a short printed summary of information, kept for quick reference.

clue.text: Innovative article removed from paper by journalist, say, when upset

parts.note: a cutting is an article clipped from a newspaper
ED is short for editor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A reporter is upset when his story is cut from the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting-edge describes the newest and most advanced work, which is innovative.

clue.text: Clash in which Indian government suffered reversal

indicators.note: reversal tells the solver to read the word backwards

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India

explanation.surface: A dispute in which the rulers of India met defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a jolt or clash, a jarring shock.

clue.text: Where landlords keep their records, we hear, in such cases

definitions.text: Where landlords keep their records, we hear, in such cases

parts.words: Where landlords keep their records, we hear, in such cases
parts.note: records here are music discs, not accounts: a pub landlord keeps them in a coin-operated machine that plays them aloud for customers

explanation.surface: Pub owners store their account books in particular cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Records look like ledgers, but they are vinyl discs; 'we hear' says they are played aloud in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin-operated record players found in pubs and cafes, which hold discs in cabinets.

clue.text: Address given after my introduction to a terribly smart set

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is introduced to a very fashionable crowd and then gives a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the person himself: after he introduces each speaker, their address follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastmaster announces speakers at a formal dinner, so their speeches follow his introductions.

clue.text: Inventor of ship reaching island without resistance

parts.note: Noah's ark was a ship

indicators.note: without means outside, so the island's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: the Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A vessel arrives at an island with no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright invented the spinning frame in the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Dramatically realistic sketch in fashionable artistic medium

indicators.note: read as fashioned, so the letters are shaped into a new order

parts.note: ink is a medium artists draw with

explanation.surface: A drawing done in trendy ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like trendy, but it is read as able to be fashioned, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen-sink drama is British realist theatre of the 1950s showing ordinary domestic life.

clue.text: Run through short London street in such underwear?

indicators.note: the piece for run goes through the middle of the street name
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: The Mall is the avenue leading to Buckingham Palace in London
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jogger dashes along a London avenue in his long johns.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MALL is the road to Buckingham Palace; 'short' drops its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal underwear is warm underclothing; such underwear is called thermal.

clue.text: Set on making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A tennis set that is back on after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set, as jelly firms up.

clue.text: On your way! Not if you do this

definitions.meaning: a rude command to go away
someone who loses their bearings is no longer on their way

explanation.definitionFit: A rude dismissal telling someone to leave, and also to lose one's way.

clue.text: After time away drink gallons for good luck!

indicators.note: says the following pieces come after the first

parts.note: a break is time away from work
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Back from holiday, someone downs several gallons for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theatrical wish used instead of 'good luck', thought unlucky to say.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's idiom wishing someone luck before a performance.

clue.text: Fencing in a state given bash

parts.note: KEN is an abbreviation for Kenya, a state in Africa
a bash is a party, or do

explanation.surface: A fight inside a country after a big party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a blow but means a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is Japanese sword fencing with bamboo staves.

clue.text: Get annoyed when lunatic swaps bishop for rook

indicators.note: swaps for says one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: batty means crazy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player gets cross when a madman exchanges pieces on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: bishop and rook are only letters B and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty means irritable; to get ratty is to become annoyed.

clue.text: Part with profits

definitions.meaning: to give up or hand over
the return or income from an investment

explanation.definitionFit: Yield means both to surrender something and the return an investment produces.

clue.text: Stir about new living in diocese recalled by fearful cardinal

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are turned round
the letter for new lives inside the word for diocese

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
to stir something about is to mix it

explanation.surface: A dreaded cardinal remembers a fuss about a new living in his diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the whole run back to front, so the stirring word ends up first. Ximenes was the Spanish cardinal of the Inquisition, and the pen name of a famous setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Ximenes led the Spanish Inquisition, which made him feared.

clue.text: Family member, one on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: SS is a steamship, the board one goes on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A relative who sits on the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: Sis is short for sister, a family member.

clue.text: Setter's forgotten expression used by irritated person

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog
something forgotten is gone from the mind

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler has forgotten an angry phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; it is the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An American exclamation of annoyance, a mild curse.

clue.text: What useless rep did — made very little money once in Italy

parts.note: a sales rep's job is selling, so what one did was sell
O, a zero, is as little as there is

explanation.surface: A poor salesman made almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A useless rep sold nothing, so SOLD O; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The soldo was an old Italian coin of small value.

clue.text: Was fan at eg Twickenham said to possess muscle?

indicators.note: the word for said holds the muscle inside it

parts.note: stated means said
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A rugby supporter is rumoured to be muscle-bound.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home of English rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch a game as a fan is to spectate at it.
